name: Velex HydroFrame Reinforced Denim
description: Heavy dark-indigo denim jeans with triple-stitched inner seams and a flexible aramid-weave lining along the inner thigh and calf — built to handle the micro-vibration and joint pressure of hydraulic leg augments without shredding at the seams after a month of use. The cut is a standard relaxed straight leg with a slightly higher rise. They look like good jeans. They last.
functionality: Inner seam reinforcement rated for sustained hydraulic joint pressure and vibration. Resists seam failure at pressure points common to hydraulic aug limbs.
what_it_says: You've burned through regular jeans with your chrome and learned from it.
worn_by: anyone who's ruined too many pairs of normal denim
story_hooks: The aramid lining is the same material used in budget ballistic gear — someone's wearing these for a reason beyond chrome compatibility.
A Tier 2 mechanic's been patching and re-patching a pair of these for three years; the patches tell a story of where she's been.
